unknowns: the Batmobile's mass: no mass property is serialized on any of the four BmAK body setups (decoded: their whole tag list is PreCachedPhysDataVersion, a bone NameProperty, one BoolProperty, AggGeom). Where it would be: SVehicle.ChassisMass, decoded at Research/BatmobileGrab/CLASS_DEFAULTS.md:434 as the class default 210.0 - a class default, not a per-vehicle authored value, and not this task's format.

the Batmobile's inertia tensor: with no mass and no tensor bytes, no box or hull formula can be evaluated on the BmAK side at all (the tool reports the formula's *shape* only). What would settle it: a decoded mass for the body plus a decision on whether the engine computes inertia from the AggGeom box (bComputedMassProperties / PrimitiveComponent field layout for the Batmobile's component), neither of which is in the files read here.

the absolute semantics of the JC3 stored diagonal: 0 of 107 single-box fleet bodies match m/12*(b^2+c^2) at 1% and 0 match the exact hull tensor, so the tensor is neither the collision box's nor the collision hull's. The residual is a near-uniform factor on all three moments (median 1.277), i.e. one scalar, which a wrong exponent would not produce. What would settle it: the render mesh of the same part, whose tensor at the stored mass would show whether the factor is a mass or an extent difference.

the third int16x4 group of the JC3 payload (+0x20..+0x27): its own exponent lane decodes its mantissas to ~1e-36, i.e. 'no products'. Whether it holds products of inertia, a principal axis, or a tag is UNKNOWN; the tool records the raw words per block.

the packing itself: value = mantissa * 2**(floor(w/128) - 111) is derived, not documented. The bias 111 is measured (group 1 must land on the hull centroid; 110 and 112 are a factor of two out), but no Havok header in this tree names the layout.

verdict.statement: BmAK's cooked body setups carry geometry only: no mass and no inertia property is serialized, and no float triple in the four AggGeom payloads is shaped like the decoded boxes' or hulls' moment tensor, so BmAK inertia is UNKNOWN. JC3's 56 hknpShapeMassProperties blocks do carry the centre of mass and the inertia diagonal (packed, bias 111), but the stored diagonal matches neither the collision hull's box formula nor its exact hull tensor: 0 of 107 single-box fleet bodies hit the box formula within 1%, with a uniform factor of about 1.277 on all three moments.
